description: Formlabs Alpha Fast resin, Form Studio 1, post-cured 2 min. Compressed between the flat platens of the Breakerspace Instron 68TM-50: the upper platen on the two prong tops, the bottom face on the lower platen. One specimen loaded to failure: peak 4.80 kN at 2.56 mm, then cracking (saw-tooth load drops) to the break at 8.66 mm. Displacement is the crosshead travel (no extensometer).
notes: The curve is soft up to 0.5 mm / 880 N (about 1.7 kN/mm, roughly 60 % of the later slope) and stiffens sharply there: one prong probably touched the platen first (prong tops not level) or the part was seating. The fit uses the straight part after that kink, 1050-1800 N (about 2.69 kN/mm); above it the resin yields (peak 4.8 kN). The material value in the statement is the datasheet's default post-cure tensile modulus (2230 MPa; flexural 2110 MPa; max-strength post-cure 2540 MPa). An ASTM D638 Type I dogbone of the same resin, also measured by crosshead, starts at about 640 N/mm: an apparent modulus of about 1.6 GPa with nominal Type I dimensions. Crosshead readings include grip seating and machine compliance, so that is a lower bound on the modulus, not a measurement of it. The data were digitized from the plot in the machine's PDF report (about +-0.01 mm, +-15 N). CalculiX elastoplastic ramp of this test (scripts/ccx_compression_ramp.py: J2 plasticity from the dogbone, large deformation, the prong tops pushed by a rigid level platen, the bottom held; results in ccx_ramp/): with a frictionless platen the prongs splay and the part collapses at 2.8-2.9 kN, far below the 4.76 kN peak; with a sticking platen it carries 4.7-4.9 kN at the test's peak travel and is still rising, so platen friction, which keeps the prongs from splaying, carries the strength. A rigid platen is also stiffer than the statement's uniform force (linear: 4018 N/mm frictionless, 4295 sticking, vs 3210), and both are stiffer than the test's 2696 N/mm: the difference needs a load-train compliance of about 1e-4 mm/N (7-11 kN/mm) or a lower modulus. Yield starts at about 0.4 kN at the sharp corners of the prongs' hex nut pockets (faces f8 with f38/f39 and f41/f42). At the test's peak load the largest tension there is 47-51 MPa (dogbone UTS 50 MPa), with 40-50 MPa bands on the lower inner surface of the bore: the likely crack sites behind the load drops after the peak.
